subject: health
title: Explicit model: body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests
focus: body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests
essentialQuestion: How do I speak up for myself, respect others, and repair a relationship after conflict?
materials: paper or a digital tool for scripts
keyPoints: Your body belongs to you; you decide about hugs, tickling, and touch, including with family.
The parts covered by a swimsuit are private.
Use correct anatomical names — they make you easier to understand and to believe.
No one should touch, look at, photograph, or ask to see your private parts, except a doctor or nurse checking your health with your guardian present, or a carer helping you when you need help.
Unsafe requests most often come from someone already known and trusted, not from a stranger — so the rule applies to everyone.
Bribes, threats, and "this is our secret" are warning signs.
If it happens it is never your fault, whatever you did, accepted, or agreed to earlier.
Tell a trusted adult and keep telling until someone helps.
privacySafeScenario: An adult a family knows well asks Sam to sit on their lap and keep it "just between us." Name every warning sign, and say exactly what Sam should do.
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: State the most important rule or fact about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests in your own words.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Scripts may be spoken, signed, typed, drawn as a comic, or acted with figures. Role-play is optional and may always be replaced by describing what a character should say and why.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about body autonomy, consent, and unsafe requests under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, review who is on your list of adults you could tell if something felt wrong. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
